title: Revitalized indeed!  🎟️OCC Invite  #broadway #musicaltheatre #comedy ...
transcript: this new Broadway show is a positive example of why I criticize so many musical comedies people often accuse me of not liking lighthearted comedies and the thing that really frustrates me is when they try to undermine or deflect the criticism by saying “it's not supposed to be high art” like “it's just supposed to be fun” because making a good musical comedy is actually really really hard and Death Becomes Her gets it right so the show is based on the film of the same name about two lifelong frenemies who both drink a magic immortality potion and this show it has what other shows have it has the dancing, the spectacle there's even a lot of cool special effects in here but what impressed me most was both the quality of,  and the balance between the character humor the situational humor and the quippy one-liners because I'll tell you the jokes here are on point but some shows rely a little too heavily on them and then they end up losing steam as they go along so I went into this blind I've actually never seen the movie and I thought the premise was super clever and it provided this great framework for unique situational comedy it always feels like the comedic tension is rising the conflict is building and you know you can give credit to the original screenplay for that but I do think it's particularly difficult to pull that off in a musical because you run the risk of the songs interfering with that pacing in this case I think because so much of the tension comes from these characters having simmering resentment and rising anger that leads them to take action are able to have these character-driven soliloquies that still feel like they're advancing the plot I recently criticized a different musical comedy for having songs that kinda felt like the same joke repeated for three minutes and people got on my case about it but this is what I mean like these songs are funny as hell but it always feels like we are progressing forward through something and on top of all of that the show is led by two of the smartest comedic actors in the theatre industry Jennifer Simard and Megan Hilty and because they've cast two actors who are incredibly skilled at the craft of comedy and not just actors who say lines loudly and expressively we can have like Megan Hilty for example playing this big cartoonish caricature of a conceited celebrity and because she's bringing her own distinct comedic sensibility to it it never feels like a stale cliche and you know one thing I'll own up to is that this isn't necessarily the genre that I find most exciting like I'm not gonna say that this is my new favorite thing or that I had the best night of my life but I did have fun and more importantly I respect game this is why the whole “it's just supposed to be fun” excuse doesn't cut it for me because you can do something that is light and campy with a high level of care and craft
reasoning: The reviewer clearly recommends the show while acknowledging it's not their preferred genre. They praise the craft, performances, and execution extensively, using it as a positive example of how musical comedy should be done.
